earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar/phonology of Ejamat (Jola-Felupe) located; Wikipedia article cites none; Crossref/searches empty.

sources.citation: Robert, Stéphane & Guillaume Segerer. 2024. Joola Keeraak. In Friederike Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa. Oxford: OUP. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780198736516.003.0011 (author version on HAL hal-01513257, 55 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 Phonology (consonants, ten vowels, phonemic length, phonotactics, syllables, vowel harmony) contains no statement on stress or accent; a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod over the whole chapter = 0 hits. NB: describes Keeraak (Kabrousse, glottocode kera1248), the sister lect of Ejamat; authors state Keeraak 'is probably not very different from the Ejamat variety' and that the Youtou/Efok/Varela/Susana area 'hosts the Ejamat (or Floupe) Joola lect'.

sources.citation: Carlton, Elizabeth Masland & Sharon Rand. 2021. Enquête sociolinguistique sur les langues diolas de Basse Casamance. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-052. Dallas: SIL International. 66 pp. (re-issue of the 1993 SIL Dakar report; wordlists also in JWAL 24(2), 1994: 85-119)
sources.note: Open SIL PDF with phonetic wordlists for Efok, Kahem and Youtou Ediamat; transcriptions may mark stress even if no rule is stated. sil.org was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ejam1238 and langdoc bibliography queries (Ejamat/Felup/ediamat/diola/joola/jóola); HAL, CrossRef, CORE, theses.fr, DICAMES, UASZ Rivières du Sud repository searches
sources.note: Bibliographic discovery only; yielded the Assine 2007/2020 Kusaanuwaay (=[eja]) records and the open Keeraak chapter; no open Ejamat description found.
